arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
# Department of Defense total nominal on-budget and off-budget outlays (in millions)
# From treasury_bulletin_2015_12_page_21.txt (FY 2011-2015)
# and treasury_bulletin_2020_12_page_24.txt (FY 2016-2020)

data = {
    2011: 678077,
    2012: 650869,
    2013: 607801,
    2014: 578013,
    2015: 562506,
    2016: 565365,
    2017: 568905,
    2018: 600705,
    2019: 653979,
    2020: 690420
}

# Sort values in ascending order
sorted_values = sorted(data.values())
print("Sorted values (in millions):")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values, 1):
    print(f"  Rank {i}: {v}")

# Calculate Hazen plotting position
# P = (i - 0.5) / n where i is rank and n is sample size
n = len(sorted_values)
print(f"\nSample size n = {n}")

# For the 85th percentile, we need to find the position P = 0.85
# Using Hazen: P = (i - 0.5) / n, so i = P * n + 0.5
percentile = 0.85
rank_approx = percentile * n + 0.5
print(f"\nHazen position for 85th percentile: {rank_approx}")

# Interpolate between ranks
i = int(rank_approx)  # floor
fraction = rank_approx - i

print(f"Interpolate between rank {i} and rank {i+1}")
print(f"Value at rank {i}: {sorted_values[i-1]}")
print(f"Value at rank {i+1}: {sorted_values[i]}")

# Linear interpolation
result = sorted_values[i-1] + fraction * (sorted_values[i] - sorted_values[i-1])

print(f"\n85th Hazen Percentile: {result}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredths: {round(result, 2)}")

# Also verify using direct formula approach
print("\n--- Verification using Hazen formula ---")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values, 1):
    P = (i - 0.5) / n
    print(f"Rank {i}: value={v}, P={P}")
EOF
